feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications/platform leader with clear domain depth and a persuasive progression at NACo. It reads professionally and is rich in relevant detail, but it is somewhat repetitive, overly dense in places, and could sharpen impact by reducing duplication and adding more outcome-focused results.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative: strong career progression within one organization supports credibility and shows increasing scope, ownership, and strategic influence.  
- Good use of scale and specificity: metrics like “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and “50+ internal publishers” add impact.  
- Relevant, modern skill mix: combines strategy, Drupal/CMS delivery, analytics, multimedia, and AI-enabled search in a way that fits senior digital roles well.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce repetition across sections: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to improve structure and scannability.  
- Add more measurable outcomes beyond activity descriptions: e.g., traffic growth, engagement lifts, efficiency gains, adoption rates, or campaign results.  
- Fix style consistency issues: mixed punctuation in lists, inconsistent use of commas before “and” (e.g., “web, email, social, and multimedia” vs other lines), and slightly awkward phrasing such as “Ranked among the top public universities…” which is unnecessary. No obvious misspellings or major grammar errors.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear seniority and domain focus. It reads well, but it’s slightly dense and overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and recent experience bullets.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten the opening and make the value proposition more outcome-oriented: “Senior digital leader with 12+ years leading public-sector web modernization, governance, analytics, and content operations for high-volume communications.”
- Replace “building the platforms” with stronger leadership language such as “leading” or “scaling” to better match director-level experience.
- Simplify the second sentence by grouping related areas and reducing the long list: “Combines enterprise web strategy, editorial systems, analytics, multimedia, and AI-enabled search to improve discovery, publishing efficiency, and audience experience.”
- Consider naming “AI-enabled search” instead of “AI-enabled user experiences” for specificity and alignment with recent projects.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Repeats themes already covered in the subtitle and Core Competencies; avoid listing too many capability areas here.
- “Multimedia production” is well supported elsewhere, so it can be shortened or deprioritized in the intro if space is tight.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block currently repeats the header and Topline Skills too closely. It would be stronger if tightened around higher-value differentiators and phrased more consistently.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and sharpen specificity: “Enterprise web modernization,” “Digital governance and editorial operations,” “Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure.”
- Prioritize the most distinctive, recent strengths: AI-enabled search, workflow automation/integrations, and public-sector communications leadership.
- Consider trimming “operations” repetition and simplifying wording for scanability.
- Possible rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integrations • Public-sector and advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream delivery

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multi-channel communications operations” overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills; consider dropping it.
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” is already well covered in Topline Skills and work history.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and repeats themes already covered in Work Experience. Tightening phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope would make it more impactful.

Suggested rewrite improvements
- Add a short lead-in such as “Selected Recent Projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Use consistent action verbs and style: e.g., “Built,” “Developed,” “Launched,” “Produced.”
- Increase specificity where possible with scale or outcome: audience, platform, campaign purpose, or measurable impact.
- Refine wording for clarity: “10 × 20-foot” and “AI-powered” or “AI-enabled” consistently; consider “bill-level chat” instead of “bill-level AI chat.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series closely overlap with current NACo roles; frame them as selected examples, not separate accomplishments.
- “Editorial storytelling,” “production,” and “distribution across website, email and social” repeat language from Work Experience; vary wording or add distinct results.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the projects footer and prior NACo roles. Tighten around consulting-level impact, platform modernization, and the AI search initiative.

Suggested edit
- Open with outcome + scope: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations, and web modernization for member-facing communications.”
- Consolidate execution bullets: combine systems/workflows/analytics/governance into one line focused on organization-wide communications operations.
- Make the Drupal work more results-oriented: “Built Drupal campaign microsites, modular storytelling components, and downloadable toolkits to support advocacy and member engagement.”
- Elevate the most distinctive item: “Led an AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval approach, structured content workflows, and discovery UX.” Add metrics if available (launch status, content indexed, time-to-publish, engagement lift).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Custom microsite structures” and AI search duplicate the Recent Projects section; keep this entry higher-level and let projects hold specifics.
- “Governance, usability, workflows, analytics” overlaps with Director of Digital Media; emphasize consultant/advisory scope instead of repeating prior responsibilities.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground the biggest outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management points already covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + leadership: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Combine and sharpen the website bullet: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership more outcome-based: add email/social growth, engagement, production volume, or campaign results if available; otherwise shorten this bullet.
- Tighten ops/analytics bullets: “Built NACo’s analytics stack across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery, improving executive reporting and decision-making” and “Implemented governance, publishing standards, and cross-department planning systems to improve consistency and efficiency.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video-program language may duplicate earlier NACo entries unless you emphasize the studio build and expanded in-house capacity.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry is too close to the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more managerial and outcomes-focused, emphasizing scale, coordination, and channel ownership without repeating website/video foundations covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite the lead to stress scope and leadership: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial execution and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Tighten bullets around distinct responsibilities:
- Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video briefing, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Built cross-functional editorial planning processes linking communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Standardized digital publishing workflows to improve consistency, coordination and turnaround time.
- If possible, add metrics: email open/click rates, video cadence/views, publishing volume, or workflow efficiency gains.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Helping scale” and “helped improve” sound soft; use direct ownership verbs.
- Avoid repeating website/team-building claims already covered in the Director and Digital Media Manager entries.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level leadership areas not already repeated elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less generic phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy & governance
- Editorial operations and publishing standards
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy and stakeholder messaging
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider swapping “content planning” for “content strategy” to sound more senior and aligned with director/consulting work.
- If space allows, make one line outcome-oriented, e.g. “Digital governance for high-volume, multi-publisher environments.”
- Keep terminology consistent with recent experience: use “governance,” “editorial operations,” and “cross-channel” rather than broader, vaguer wording.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “editorial systems and governance” duplicate Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” is already reinforced across the header and multiple NACo roles.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill coverage, but this item is too tool-heavy and overlaps heavily with the Technical + IT section. In Topline Skills, it should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and modernization themes tied to recent Drupal/AI work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a software list to a capability-led line: “Drupal platform leadership • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API and workflow integrations • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery”
- Remove lower-priority or older platforms from this topline item unless central to target roles; keep WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages in Technical + IT instead.
- Drop “jQuery” here; it reads dated and is better suited to Technical + IT if retained at all.
- If space allows, make impact more explicit: “Drupal modernization for 10,000+ pages” or “platforms supporting 3.5M annual page views” in experience bullets, not here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Significant overlap with “Technical + IT” Web Platforms & CMS and Coding & Technical Implementation.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies and the header summary; keep wording distinct.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for the most recent digital leadership work, but it reads as a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with “Technical + IT.” Make it more outcome-oriented and slightly more strategic.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio and Microsoft Clarity • Analytics infrastructure and dashboarding • KPI framework design • Executive/leadership reporting • SEO, UX and performance analysis”
- Group tools first, then capabilities; this improves scanability and makes the section feel less like a duplicate software inventory.
- Replace “optimization” with clearer business value via “KPI framework design” and “executive/leadership reporting.”
- If accurate, consider adding one stronger impact phrase elsewhere in the CV tied to this skill set, e.g., “built analytics infrastructure supporting strategic decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Core Competencies: Analytics and reporting infrastructure” and “Technical + IT: Data, Analytics & Optimization.”
- Avoid repeating every tool in all three places; keep Topline Skills strategic, Technical + IT tool-specific.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it’s generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize higher-level production capability and recent leadership impact rather than listing basic tasks/tools.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from task list to capability statement: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • In-house studio operations • PTZ camera systems and multi-camera workflows • Virtual event production”
- Consider replacing “Video production and editing” with “Broadcast-quality video production” to better match the studio-building achievement in the 2022–2024 role.
- Combine “Livestreaming” and “Hybrid and virtual event production” into one stronger phrase to reduce fragmentation.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie this skill area to outcomes from recent roles (e.g., built in-house studio, expanded advocacy programming, supported recurring video series).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same wording.
- Tool-level detail like PTZ/studio workflows also appears in Technical + IT, so keep this section focused on strategic capability.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too bare and duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills section. This item should either add specificity on level of use or be tightened to emphasize the most current, highest-value platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages** is fine, but consider leading with depth: **Drupal (enterprise migration, modular builds) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add brief qualifiers instead of just names: **Drupal (10,000+ page migration) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If you want cleaner phrasing, rename the heading to **CMS & Web Platforms** for slightly stronger readability.
- Keep only platforms you can credibly discuss in interviews; if GitHub Pages is minor, remove it.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps heavily with **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider consolidating or differentiating this section with proficiency/context.
- Drupal already appears repeatedly in recent experience, so avoid over-weighting older or less-used platforms here.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical range, but this reads like a generic keyword dump and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. For a senior digital leader, emphasize implementation depth and modern tools rather than basic languages alone.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe for level and specificity: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery”
- Group by function to improve scanability: “Integrations & deployment: API integrations, Google Tag Manager, GitHub Actions, Cloudflare Workers”
- If accurate, add scope/outcome context elsewhere or inline via parenthetical examples, e.g. “API integrations (CMS, analytics, campaign tools)” or “GitHub Actions (deployment automation)”
- Consider dropping versioned basics (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) in favor of “HTML/CSS” to save space and reduce junior-level feel

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills; keep the stronger version in one place
- GTM also overlaps conceptually with analytics infrastructure elsewhere, so avoid repeating it if space is tight

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow leadership. Since workflow automation already appears in Core Competencies and Topline Skills, this item should be tighter and more clearly grouped to avoid repetition.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe by function, not just brand names: “Automation & workflow systems: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier; project/work management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp; collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams.”
- Put the strongest, most relevant tools first: Airtable, Power Automate, and Zapier should lead because they align with your recent systems/automation work.
- Consider trimming lower-value collaboration tools if space is tight; Slack and Teams are widely assumed unless central to your workflow design.
- If possible, connect to impact elsewhere in the CV with a brief qualifier such as “used to support cross-team publishing, approvals, and reporting workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” already appears in Core Competencies and Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same concept without adding specificity.
- Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp overlap heavily; listing all four may feel redundant unless each was materially used.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Relevant tools, but this item is too generic and misses the scale/ownership shown in recent roles. It should signal enterprise email operations rather than read like a basic software list.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten and order by strongest/recent relevance: **Higher Logic • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope in brief parentheticals: **Higher Logic (newsletter/member communications)** • **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (campaign automation)** • **Mailchimp (smaller-scale campaigns)**
- If space allows elsewhere, connect to outcomes rather than tools alone, e.g., “supported newsletters reaching tens of thousands” or “managed multi-newsletter/member communications operations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with work experience bullets already covering email leadership; avoid repeating channel scale here unless you convert those bullets to focus more on strategy/governance.
- “Engagement Systems” may feel vague next to “Multi-channel communications operations” in Core Competencies; “Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms” is clearer.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills” and the Director role. As a Technical + IT item, it should be tighter, more tool-specific, and avoid generic capability terms.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with: **GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Google Search Console • Google Optimize / A/B testing platforms**
- Swap broad nouns like **SEO**, **A/B testing**, and **Dashboarding** for either tools or sharper labels: **SEO analysis**, **experiment design**, **executive reporting dashboards**
- Order by strongest/recently evidenced tools first: **GA4, Clarity, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio**
- If space allows, add one qualifier tied to impact elsewhere in CV: **analytics stack for enterprise reporting and optimization**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates **Topline Skills → Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider keeping tools here and leaving KPI/reporting language in Topline Skills.
- “Dashboarding” repeats the reporting emphasis already covered in recent NACo experience.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and repeats themes covered more clearly in later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and, if possible, quantify outputs or scale.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize early-career buildout and concrete delivery: “Promoted across two digital roles while helping establish NACo’s first in-house digital team and improve publishing workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add specific outputs/results if available: website size/traffic at the time, number of livestreams or weekly videos produced, audience reach, event volume, or team size supported.
- Tighten the second sentence to highlight ownership: “Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and provided day-to-day supervision for a digital media associate.”
- If accurate, replace “high-impact” with evidence-based language such as “recurring,” “organization-wide,” or quantified reach.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Strengthening workflows” overlaps with the 2018–2022 and 2022–2024 roles; keep this version lighter and more tactical.
- “Weekly video updates” is echoed in the Associate Communications Director role; distinguish this as launching/producing rather than expanding.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows the start of your multimedia/digital trajectory, but it reads generic and underplays the podcast launch. Since later roles already cover broad digital production, this item should emphasize innovation/program support plus the “first podcast” achievement.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout outcome: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county-focused programs and policy priorities; launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with a clearer scope: “Produced digital and multimedia materials to support program communications and policy storytelling.”
- If possible, add one measurable detail: number of episodes launched, audience/downloads, stakeholder groups served, or number/type of research projects coordinated.
- Keep it to 1–2 lines; this is an older role, so concise impact is better than broad responsibility lists.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating generic “digital content production/multimedia” language already covered more strongly in later NACo roles.
- Don’t overemphasize video/editorial operations here; later entries show that progression more credibly.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but reads as a mixed list of software and capabilities. It also overlaps with “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” and multiple work-experience bullets, so it should stay concise and tool-focused.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: **Creative & Production Tools**
